facts.text: Middle Frisco originally part of the Frisco Plazas, established in the 1860s by Hispanic families for livestock grazing and formalized as a village around 1880.
Middle Frisco evolved from Middle San Francisco Plaza to its current name in the early 20th century, reflecting Anglo-American naming trends.
The 1884 Frisco War, a range conflict between Texas cattle ranchers and Hispanic sheepherders, centered around Middle Frisco.
Francis of Assisi Church, built in 1880, stands as one of Middle Frisco's oldest structures and a focal point of community faith.
Middle Frisco lies within the vast Gila National Forest, surrounded by creeks, ranchlands, and forested hills that once supported early sawmilling operations.
Early Hispanic pioneers in Middle Frisco built communal irrigation systems along the San Francisco River Valley, using traditional Spanish colonial practices to sustain farming.
